scope: Phase four: color, vector, quaternion, Euler/angle, matrix, bounding-box and rectangle editing
status: Implemented; all functional regressions pass; final implementation pair and same-program control exceed the timing variation limit
implemented: The existing ParameterValue model now covers basic and fixed-size numeric values. Native type selection, component order, range checks, conversion and undo data records remain in the core.
Public C interface version 11 adds borrowed/copied finite real arrays. It exposes no STL, SDK, SDL or native pointer data. Common copying enforces null/count, finite-number and aggregate size limits.
Typed metadata includes rows, columns, column labels, row labels, scale and native type identity. Generic field borrowing is shared by the application and the native working-copy editor.
Built-in renderers and independent modules use the same query/value/command path. Open native dialogs retain the selected query, renderer, modification command and choice provider.

Inline component drags retain a draft and commit once. Native dialogs retain owned working copies and a pre-interaction value per row; Escape or child-picker cancellation restores that value. Apply groups all rows into one undo step. Input activity includes a cancelled interaction so Escape cannot also close its containing dialog after ImGui ends the active widget.
Color picking has explicit confirmation/cancellation; the renderer only tracks popup opening/closing. Value restoration belongs to the application draft or the native working-copy owner.

Turn/degree controls, RGBA byte-channel controls, quaternion component editing, matrix collapse, rectangle representations and native object picking remain available. Rectangle representation belongs to its editing row.
Custom numeric/geometric parameter types select the nearest ordinary parent editor while retaining their actual GUID. No SDK source or viewport rendering/transfer implementation changed.

full_ctest.note: All 124 tests passed on the final production source, including the five new UI cases and the held-mouse Escape cancellation regression. No tests skipped.

checks.core_cases: Repeated updates across all eight compound shapes, cancel/Redo preservation, native working copies, component count/range/finite validation, inherited native type identity, real-array lifetime and completed-operation output copying.

retained_diagnostics.result: The first new module run passed 26/28. The native color swatch used ColorButton, which lacked the named test item used by the previous swatch; its original InvisibleButton drawing was restored. Test cleanup now closes owned test popups, preventing a failed modal test from blocking a following inline drag. The module rerun and final targeted run pass all 29 cases after adding the held-mouse cancellation regression.
An attempted alternation-style filter selected no native UI cases; the complete module group was used instead. This rejected invocation is not counted as a pass.
First same-program control exceeded the original MAD limit; retained, not accepted.

This repeat used the earlier identical source, binary, scene, warmup and sampling. It exceeded the MAD limit. After the later cancellation fix, a fresh implementation pair and one same-program control were recorded separately.

retained_diagnostics.cause: The original value was saved and restored correctly. Escape ended the ImGui active widget before the renderer returned, so the parent also interpreted Escape as dialog cancellation and deleted the working parameter. Clearing ActiveID alone did not fix this.
retained_diagnostics.fix: The native draft owner retains the start value from activation or the first write, restores it on cancellation, and reports the cancelled interaction as active for that frame. A held-mouse regression verifies that the dialog remains open and later mouse movement does not write.
